newsitem.title: USA: Ten-year spreads favor dlr after JGB, Bund moves.
newsitem.headline: Ten-year spreads favor dlr after JGB, Bund moves.

text.p: Wider spreads between U.S. and Japanese interest rates will be a boon for the dollar versus the yen after Japanese government bond (JGB) yields hit record lows this week, global investment strategists said.
Moreover, the recent contraction of differentials between yields on 10-year U.S. and German bonds should be temporary and will not detract from investments in the U.S. fixed income market, they said.
"Over time, the dollar is still in really good shape," said Hamilton Davis, vice president of taxable fixed income at Everen Securities, a global investment firm.
"Yield differentials and the positive spread our 10-year Treasuries have over both JGBs and bunds are going to be something that are favorable for Treasuries, generally speaking."
The dollar came under pressure, trading below 1.70 marks early this week, as the yield premium that 10-year Treasury notes offer over 10-year bunds fell below 100 basis points.
But international bond experts said the narrower gap was a temporary detour after T-note/bund differentials ballooned from around 60 to 116 points since the beginning of the year.
"I still think over time dollar-denominated securities are going to attract attention," said Davis. "We had that quick widening out and I just think we're coming back to a bit more normal levels."
U.S./German yield spreads have steadily moved in favor of the dollar since 1995 when German long-term interest rates were about 65 basis points above similar duration U.S. rates, experts said.

With the market expecting that U.S. economic strength will eventually lead to a tightening of short-term U.S. rates, 10-year Treasury yields are also expected to rise from their current level around 6.70 percent.

But Germany lacks such an economic spur to raise rates, and experts said the German yield curve should flatten after a recent spark of optimism about European growth prospects dims and bund yields fall again after rising above 5.70 percent this week.

"I would say you are at the high end of what you could expect in terms of rates being priced in the (German) curve," said Richard Koss, an international strategist at MFR Inc, an investment advisory firm.
The 10-year bund/Treasury gap widened to 107 points in Europe on Friday.
Meanwhile, the return on 10-year JGBs was a paltry 2.23 percent in late Japanese trade on Friday, giving Treasuries a juicy yield advantage of about 4.46 percentage points.

While temporary repatriation of offshore investments back to yen before Japan's March 31 fiscal yearend may have helped to support Japanese bonds, pushing interest rates lower this week, analysts said they would not rule out JGB yields falling below 2.0 percent at some point.
As it stands now, wider U.S./Japan spreads have already raised expectations for dollar/yen.

Ron Leven, a currency strategist at J.P. Morgan, said dollar/yen is more sensitive to 10-year bond spreads than dollar/mark. "The widening spread has sort of raised the resistance level up roughly a yen and a half, from around 123 yen to 124.50 yen. So, in that sense it is constructive for dollar/yen," he said.

But MFR's Koss said short-term dollar/yen movements are less well correlated to changes in interest rate spreads because Japan's trade surplus and a shaky Japanese stock market have strengthened politician's resolve to keep dollar/yen below 125.
"It's going to be an interesting tussle on that side, between the political will and just the sheer force of interest rate differences," Koss said.
Near 1100 EST/1600 GMT on Friday, dollar/yen was trading at 123.32/43, down from 123.40/45 at the open and the dollar was changing hands at 1.6985/90 marks, slightly off from 1.7050/60.
